why: The must_catch list has one item: line 1 must FAIL because the app would start on defaults and nobody would learn which file is broken or where the mistake is. The output marks line 1 "FAIL". Its evidence says that since src/app.js spreads the result over DEFAULTS, "a typo in config.json now starts the app silently on port 8080 / greeting 'hi'". It also says "no message at all says which file is wrong or where", which it ties back to the requester's complaint. The wrong_build section makes the same point again: "prints 'listening on 8080' using defaults... can't tell which file is broken or where the typo is." Both parts of the trap are covered: the app starts on defaults, and the user learns neither the file nor the location, which goes against what the request asked for.
